statement: If an odd number by multiplying an even number make some number, the product will be even.
heath_proof: For let the odd number A by multiplying the even number B make C; I say that C is even. For, since A by multiplying B has made C, therefore C is made up of as many numbers equal to B as there are units in A. [VII. Def. 15] And B is even; therefore C is made up of even numbers. But, if as many even numbers as we please be added together, the whole is even. [IX. 21] Therefore C is even.

9.28
**Statement:** If an odd number by multiplying an even number make some number, the product will be even.

**Step 1.** Let A be an odd number and B be an even number, and let C be the product A times B. We are to show that C is even.

**Step 2.** By the definition of multiplication [D7.15], A times B means that B is added to itself as many times as there are units in A. That is, C = B + B + ... + B, where the number of summands is equal to A.

**Step 3.** Since B is even [given], each of the A summands in this sum is an even number.

**Step 4.** We have as many even numbers as we please (namely A copies of B) added together. By Proposition 9.21, if as many even numbers as we please be added together, the whole is even. Therefore C, being the sum of A even numbers, is even.

**Step 5.** Therefore, if an odd number by multiplying an even number make some number, the product will be even. Q.E.D.
